t: You are looking at Boone's Chapel, a very small single-storey building of 1683. It is attributed to Sir Christopher Wren. The walls are red brick, with Portland stone around the windows and at the corners, under a pyramid-shaped roof topped by an open wooden cupola. It measures just 45 square metres. It is listed Grade I, the highest category on the National Heritage List for England. Wren is best known for St Paul's Cathedral, but here you see his work at its smallest.
